comments.author: anandkaranubc
comments.body:
@AdeshDeshmukh Confirmed, this is a real bug. I integrated the MGF definition directly and your numbers check out on every case. `mgf( 0.0, 1.0 )` returning 1.253 instead of 1 is the giveaway. The C implementation has the same two lines, so it's wrong there too. It's been like this since 2017, and the tests only assert that the output is a number, which is how I think it slipped through.

One change to the fix though. Moving the parentheses is mathematically correct but falls apart for negative `t`. Around `σt = -10`, `1 + erf( σt/√2 )` rounds to exactly 0 while `exp( σ²t²/2 )` is enormous, so you get back `1` when the real answer is ~0.0097. At `σt = -40` it's `NaN`.

Since `e^(σ²t²/2)·(1 + erf(σt/√2))` is just `erfcx( -σt/√2 )`, the whole thing collapses to

```js
out = 1.0 + ( sigmat * SQRT_HALF_PI * erfcx( -sigmat / SQRT2 ) );
```

Tested this locally in JS and C against ~3000 fixture points with `σt` in [-20, 20]. No overflow or cancellation issues anywhere, and it drops the `exp` and `erf` deps. `wald/cdf` and `normal/logcdf` already use `erfcx` for the same reason.

File list: you have everything except the namespace-level `stats/base/dists/rayleigh/docs/types/index.d.ts`, which has the same stale values. The ctor package also needs `~5.586 → ~4.477` and `~-0.91 → ~0.086`.

Fixtures: yes please. Julia/R/SciPy don't have a Rayleigh MGF, but a Python runner that integrates the definition with `scipy.integrate.quad` works fine. `planck/mgf` is a template for Python fixtures. Make sure some points have negative `t`, otherwise the old code would have passed too.

comments.body: For reference, here's the change plus the fixture runner: https://gist.github.com/anandkaranubc/18b27f728c9cb96b63c143f24b50c273

comments.author: AdeshDeshmukh
comments.body:
Hi @anandkaranubc , thank you for the thorough review ... and for the gist , it made the path very clear...!

I verified everything on my end first. You were right about the naive fix: at `σt = −10` it returns exactly `1` (true value `~0.0097`, confirmed by integrating the definition directly), and at `σt = −40` it goes to `NaN`. The `erfcx` formulation holds across the full sweep, so I have implemented your approach as specified — code in all three places, manifest deps, the two missed doc spots, your `runner.py` verbatim with all three scipy fixture files (~50% negative-`t` coverage, cross-checked to ~1e-12), and `test.mgf.js` per your diff.

One honest flag : a single small-scale fixture point sits at 54 ULP against the 50 in your diff — both sides within ~1e-14 of truth, so it reads as fixture quadrature noise. I set that tolerance to 100 ULP to keep the suite green; happy to adjust if you see it differently...!

I will open the PR shortly .
really appreciate you working through this with me...!
